title: How the Internet & SaaS security policies troubleshooting runbook scopes a case to Malware Protection, ATP or Sandbox and what support asks for
aliases: Internet & SaaS Security Policies Support Troubleshooting Runbook

prose.label: Where the symptoms go.
prose.text: Malware Protection and ATP block and allow checks and the Unscannable Files rules are in [[zia.troubleshooting.security-policies-runbook.malware-atp]]. Sandbox symptoms are in [[zia.troubleshooting.security-policies-runbook.sandbox]].

cve-route.statement: For a query about Zscaler's protection against a specific CVE or vulnerability, the runbook says to search the ThreatLabz Product Security Advisories for the CVE number or keyword.

quotes: See Zscaler ’s Threatlabz’s Product Security Advisories and search for a matching CVE number or keyword.
If you have a query with Zscaler’s protection against a specific CVE or vulnerability, complete the following steps.

detection-disagreement.statement: When an admin disagrees with Zscaler's detection of a URL or file, the runbook says to export the Web Insights logs with all fields selected, check Zulu (Reanalyze an existing verdict), search the Threat Library by threat name, check VirusTotal (noting the verdict and recording its URL), and submit the files to the Sandbox Scanning Portal; it then states that the maximum size for one file is 20 MB.

quotes: If you disagree with the Zscaler detection result for a specific URL or file, export the Web Insights logs with all fields selected for the respective destinations
Go to your Zulu account and enter the URL to find the verdict from Zscaler. Click Reanalyze if an existing verdict is found.
Go to Zscaler Threat Library portal and search using the threat name.
Take note of the verdict and record the VirusTotal’s URL post analysis completion.
Go to Zscaler Sandbox Scanning Portal and submit the files for analysis.
The maximum size for one file is 20 MB.

three-controls.statement: The runbook lists Malware Protection, Advanced Threat Protection (ATP) and Sandbox as the security controls, and uses Web Insights log information to scope which control is involved.

quotes: Zscaler’s security controls include Malware Protection, Advanced Threat Protection (ATP), and Sandbox.
Using the information in Web Insights logs helps to scope the security controls involved and provide troubleshooting guidance to isolate the cause of potential policy misbehavior.

sandbox-support-data.statement: The runbook's closing Further Steps list, after the Sandbox section, asks for screenshots of the Sandbox policy configuration and the Advanced Threat Protection Exception configuration, for the Web Insights logs with all fields selected, and to temporarily enable Remote Assistance.

quotes: The Web Insights logs with all fields selected.

malware-atp-support-data.conditions: Quoted from the Further Steps list of the access-allowed-unexpectedly section. The access-blocked-unexpectedly section's Further Steps list reads the same items in the capture, but identical text in the two sections makes a separate quote ambiguous.
malware-atp-support-data.statement: For Malware Protection and ATP cases, the runbook's Further Steps list asks for screenshots of the Malware Policy & Exception configuration and the Advanced Threat Protection Policy & Exception configuration, the Web Insights logs with all fields selected, and to temporarily enable Remote Assistance.

quotes: Advanced Threat Protection Policy & Exception configuration.
Web Insights logs with all fields selected.
evidence.after: For Advanced Threat Protection Policy configuration, check for any matching entry in Security Exceptions by going to Security Exceptions > Do Not Scan Content from these URLs.

policy-block-reasons.statement: For a policy block action, the runbook refers to Policy Reasons.

quotes: For policy block action, see Policy Reasons.

policy-reasons-content.title: What Allow to Differentiate means in the unexpected-block example
policy-reasons-content.detail: The runbook's unexpected-block example mentions an Allow to Differentiate policy without defining it. The Policy Reasons article it points to is captured as zscaler-help zia-policy-reasons.json and its values are in the web log type and [[zia.logs.web-field-semantics]]; a search of that capture for 'Differentiate' returned nothing.
